answer: Anchor each identity to a single ferrous key sealed in a tamper-resistant chip, and record its standing in a timber ledger that grows one ring per epoch only after verified work. Each epoch a sparrow — a randomly drawn peer — re-derives one past task from the ledger and checks it step by step. An honest agent anchors once and passes cheaply. An attacker with a thousand fakes must buy a thousand chips, forge a thousand timber histories, and survive a thousand sparrow audits every epoch, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake.
